Condo Sinking Fund and Common Area Fees

Ownership costs after you buy
HomeGuidesCondo Sinking Fund and Common Area Fees

Ownership and costs · Last reviewed: 2026-11-23

After you buy a condo you pay ongoing costs to maintain the shared parts of the building. Two items appear most often: a recurring common area fee and a sinking fund. Amounts differ by project, so this guide shows what we have recorded from developer materials and how to compare them.

Juristic person and what it does

A registered condominium has a juristic person that manages the common property: lifts, pool, gardens, security, cleaning and insurance. Owners pay for it through fees decided under the building’s rules.

Common area fee

The common area fee, often called CAM, is billed monthly or yearly. Many Phuket condos bill it per square metre of the unit, others use a fixed amount. Ask what it covers (water, cleaning, security, pool) and what is billed separately (electricity, internet, parking).

Sinking fund

The sinking fund is a reserve for large future repairs and replacements. It is commonly a one-off payment at transfer, though some buildings collect it over time. Ask how it is held and who can spend it.

Example for orientation only: a project that charges THB 70 per square metre per month, for a unit of 50 square metres, would bill THB 3,500 per month. Use the real figure and the real unit size for your case.

How to compare projects

  • Convert every fee to a monthly amount for your unit size.
  • Ask what services the fee includes and how often it has changed.
  • Ask whether the building has a sinking fund balance and how it is audited.
  • Compare the fee with the amenities: a large pool and gym cost more to run.

Frequently asked questions

Is the sinking fund refundable?

Usually not when you sell: it is part of the building’s reserve. Confirm the rule for the building.

Can the fee go up?

Yes. Fees are decided by the juristic person and owners under the building’s rules. Ask for the history.
